## Rules

- **History is BUDGETED, never sliced** (chat v1.146.0, agents v1.152.0). Both
  chat lanes call `_plan_context` → `context.plan_history`; the perceive→act
  loop calls `context.agent_window.plan_agent_transcript` once per step. Both
  fit the transcript to the answering model's window (`_context_window`: pin →
  measured envelope (v1.201.0, probed/partial/tuned profiles only — seeded and
  trusted never speak here) → fleet probe → default) and report what they
  dropped. Do not reintroduce a fixed
  `messages[-N:]`, and if you add to the system prompt, add it BEFORE the
  planner runs or its cost is invisible to the budget.

- **Compaction is MODEL-written and LEDGER-checked** (v1.153.0). `context/
  compaction.py` lets a model write a real structured summary of the older
  conversation, then removes every line carrying a claim the record will not
  support: file paths must appear in the transcript or in
  `agents/outcome.session_result` (derived from `ToolInvocation` +
  `UndoJournal`), and quoted spans must appear verbatim. A summary that
  survives verification empty is NOT shown — the deterministic recap keeps the
  job. Same honest-mock rule as skill distill: no real model ⇒ no summary,
  because this text is injected into the system prompt of every later turn and
  read back as authoritative. The two lanes differ by who is present: chat
  SIGNALS at `SUGGEST_AT` (0.70) and lets the user choose via
  `POST /chat/compact`, and only acts alone at `AUTO_AT` (~0.92); an agent run
  has nobody to ask, so it compacts itself at the ceiling and emits
  `context.compacted`. Pressure is measured on RAW demand (`raw_tokens`), never
  on the planned transcript — that fits by construction and so can never report
  the 70% the whole feature keys off. Coverage always restarts from the
  beginning and feeds the previous summary back in as `prior`; covering only
  the new blocks would silently discard everything the first summary said.

- **An assistant turn and its `role="tool"` results are ONE unit** (v1.152.0).
  Any code that trims, slices, or replays an agent transcript must move them
  together — a `tool_use` without its `tool_result` makes strict providers
  reject the ENTIRE conversation, so a context fix that splits them is worse
  than the overflow it prevents. `plan_agent_transcript` sacrifices in order:
  stale tool output → whole blocks (oldest first) → the task itself, clipped.
  The task is `messages[0]` and is never dropped; dropped work is summarized
  into the SYSTEM prompt, never injected as fake assistant turns.

- **Keep big results OUT of the context, don't trim them after** (v1.159.0).
  `repl/` is a per-session persistent Python namespace (a subprocess speaking
  newline-JSON, spawned by re-executing the app itself via the hidden
  `repl-worker` subcommand — `run_code` uses `shutil.which("python")` and so
  cannot run Python at all on a packaged install). Any tool call may carry
  `_store_as="name"`: `registry.invoke` strips it, binds the result into that
  session's namespace and returns a ONE-LINE RECEIPT, and the `repl` tool then
  reaches the value by name. A 5,000-entry listing becomes `len(files)` and a
  slice. This is the counterpart to the budget (v1.152.0) and compaction
  (v1.153.0): those decide what to throw away once a payload has arrived, this
  decides what never has to arrive. The value crosses as a JSON string LITERAL,
  never interpolated as code — a tool result must not be executable. `repl` is
  on the DENY FLOOR and defaults to `ask`: it runs model-written code AND the
  namespace persists for a whole session, so consent to one call is not consent
  to what accumulates. `_store_as` is advertised only on `VERBOSE_TOOLS` —
  putting it on all ~60 tools would spend more context than the feature saves.

- **The REPL's writes are CONFINED; its reads are not** (v1.160.0). Every file
  tool routes through `core/fs_policy`; the `repl` child routed through nothing,
  and it was measurable — `read_file` refused the app's own Fernet key while a
  cell printed it, and a cell writing to an absolute path outside the workspace
  succeeded while `created_paths` said `[]`, because that diff only ever scans
  INSIDE the workspace. An invisible write is worse than an untidy one.
  `repl/worker.install_confinement` arms a `sys.addaudithook` before any cell
  runs; `repl/session.confinement_env` computes the policy from `fs_policy`
  (the worker is stdlib-only and cannot import it). READS STAY BROAD ON
  PURPOSE — the user's tax documents live all over the disk and a REPL that
  cannot open them is a worse tool — so only protected roots and an explicit
  `IRONJARVIS_FS_ALLOWLIST` restrict reading. WRITES pin to the workspace (the
  grounded project's folder when chat resolved one) plus a PRIVATE scratch dir:
  the whole system temp root would expose every other program's temp files, and
  with no redirect at all `tempfile` probes, fails, and silently falls back to
  `os.getcwd()` — filling the user's project with `tmpXXXX` files. Subprocess
  spawning and NEW `ctypes` loads are refused because each walks around the
  rule; `ctypes` is imported BEFORE the hook is armed, since Windows evaluates
  `windll.kernel32` at import time and a blanket refusal breaks `import ctypes`
  itself. `PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE` is set for tidiness, NOT correctness —
  `importlib` swallows a refused `.pyc` write. Be honest in any doc you write
  about this: an audit hook inside the interpreter it polices is a guardrail
  against a careless model, NOT a sandbox against hostile code.

- `repl/` — the session NAMESPACE (v1.159.0). `worker.py` is the child:
  stdlib-only (it is spawned from a frozen binary), newline-JSON on
  stdin/stdout, one persistent globals dict, output capped and truncation
  reported. `session.py` is the parent: one child per session, every
  blocking step through `asyncio.to_thread`, a reader thread so a deadline
  can actually be honoured, kill-on-timeout, and an honest `restarted` flag
  so a model is never told its variables survived when they did not.
  `tools/repl_tool.py` is the tool. Do not add a `get()`-first path: the
  registry creates a namespace on demand through `execute`, and a
  `get()`-first caller fails on the FIRST call of every session. Namespaces
  are keyed by `namespace_key(session_id, workspace)` — one per (session,
  FOLDER) pair, because chat runs every turn as session id `"chat"` while its
  workspace follows the grounded project, so keying on the id alone pinned the
  write root to whichever project opened first. The registry's PUBLIC surface
  (`get`/`dispose`/`sweep`/`session_ids`/`in`) still speaks session ids and
  covers every folder that session used; only the internal dict key is
  composite.

- `context/` — `budget.plan_history`: the per-turn CHAT history planner (pure,
  offline, deterministic recap), consumed by both chat lanes.
  `agent_window.plan_agent_transcript`: the same job for an agent RUN, and a
  separate module because it protects the oldest message (the task) instead of
  the newest, and because tool pairs are indivisible. Shares `budget.py`'s
  token estimator and reserves so both lanes count tokens identically.
  `compaction.py` is the layer above both: thresholds, the structured prompt,
  and the verification pass that makes a model-written summary admissible.
  `store.py` caches one summary per covered prefix, CONTENT-ADDRESSED (a chat
  turn carries no thread id, an unsaved thread has none, and a forked thread
  should inherit its parent's summary for free) — and it is registered in
  `core.db._LATE_MODEL_MODULES`, without which its lazily-created table lands
  on fresh test DBs and on no real install (the v1.151.2 lesson).

- **A long chat keeps every message: the oldest MOVE to the chat's older messages, never deleted** (v1.499.3 review). The live window stays 200; what leaves it moves in the same transaction to `chatoldermessage` (`chat_append.leaving_live_window` + `keep_older`; kept live when it cannot be kept), is indexed for history search (negative `seq`) and is read by `GET /chat/threads/{id}/older`. The compaction header says only "the full conversation is still stored". The chat page reads them back as the reader scrolls up (48-a, see `docs/rules/chat.md`). Phone chats, coding sessions and round-tables keep theirs too since 48-b (the next entry). OPEN: a rebuilt index does not re-add older docs (48-c). Pins: `tests/test_review_fixes_chat_v1499_3.py`, `tests/test_search_sync.py`.

- **Phone chats, coding sessions and round-tables keep every message too: no store cuts at its cap, and the cut part MOVES in the same write** (v1.584.0, 48-b, build-out plan R2.14, idea 48, D-48.1).
  `comm/threads.CommThreadStore.append` (live 200), `harness/sessions._with_lines` (live 200, still the whole-turn cut of `_capped`; `append_lines`, `take_wait`, and `create_with_lines` for a branch) and `agents/threads.AgentThreads._append` (live 400) call `context/older_messages.ensure_older_table` BEFORE their transaction and `keep_older(db, record, moved, kind=)` inside it, into the one `chatoldermessage` store keyed by the thread id; when it cannot keep (no table, a fault) the lines stay live, never dropped (pinned for all three kinds, both faults). The STORE lives in `context/older_messages` (table, keep, count, read, drop, `older_by_who`), below every writer: `agents/`, `comm/` and `harness/` never import `daemon/` for it (`test_remember_ladder_shared_v1185` pins `agents/threads`), and `daemon/chat_append` re-exports its names; the boot entry in `core.db._LATE_MODEL_MODULES` is `..context.older_messages`, pinned by name. `keep_older` writes every row out before it adds any (a fault leaves nothing half-kept). A coding session's older lines are never in Chat's history search (`surface == "build"`); a phone chat's are (`kind="comm"`), a room's under its project (`kind="round"`, `agents/threads._room_for_older`). A rewind cuts only the live lines, and a rewind to the first LIVE question of a session that keeps older lines leaves its name (it is not back to nothing; `cut_transcript`). Delete drops them in the same transaction: `routes/chat.delete_thread` (phone chats, coding sessions) and `AgentThreads.delete`. `GET /build/sessions/{id}` (every `_full_view` answer) carries `older`, read with a fresh copy of the row under the conversation lock (`_with_older`), and the Code view (`components/harness/HarnessSession`) takes it WITH the view (`takeView`, one update; the first view an opening takes starts over at its count when nothing is held, so opening reads nothing earlier) and pages `GET /chat/threads/{id}/older` through `lib/olderMessages` and `components/chat/OlderMessages`, rows drawn by `HarnessMessageRow` `readOnly` (no Rewind, Branch, Retry, Keep, Answer these, Show me, suggestion, client question, door or Undo); a phone chat is the chat page's (48-a) as it was. The start is claimed per kind (`chat_append.start_kept_of`): a chat by v1.499.4's time; a phone chat or coding session by `core.db.older_kept_since`, the time this database was first opened by a version that keeps them (`_ironjarvis_meta` key `older_kept_since`, written once by `init_db`, never moved; missing or unreadable is "not known"), and a coding session never by "fewer than the cap" (its live lines shrink by turn cuts and rewinds). The R0.1 left-out count includes older rows: `CommThreadStore.history_window` adds `older_messages.older_by_who` (the inbound phone lane calls it off the loop), and a round shown the room itself counts the room's (`AgentThreads.older_by_who`, once a round, off the loop), only those below where its live messages started when the round read the room (`_get_with_older`, one read under the conversation lock; one the round's own appends moved since was passed, never also counted). The model is sent only the live window, budgeted as before. A ROOM'S kept messages are read on its own page (`components/agents/mission/RoomTranscript`, `/agents?thread=<id>`, where a "round" history hit and the bell land): `GET /agents/threads/{id}` answers `older`, read with the room under the conversation lock, and `GET /agents/threads/{id}/older` pages them (the chat route's shape; `/chat/threads/{id}/older` stays 404 for a room); a room's start is `start_kept_of(room=True, cap=400)` (its live messages only grow, so under 400 with nothing older proves the start). That page opens at its top, so its line loads only when PRESSED (reaching it reads nothing). The tops name their own thing (`OLDER_WORDS`): **Start of this chat**, **Start of this session** (the Code view), **Start of this conversation** (a room). A coding session's count never goes down, so a LOWER one is a stale view answered late: `lib/olderMessages.keepBefore` keeps the rows held before it, never starts over. A round's own appends (`run_round`) run off the loop (`asyncio.to_thread`); the phone lane's `InboundPoller._safe_append` still writes on the loop (older than 48-b, OPEN). Pins: `tests/test_older_messages_everywhere.py`, `dashboard/__tests__/code-scroll-back-48b.test.tsx`, `dashboard/__tests__/room-scroll-back-48b.test.tsx`, `dashboard/__tests__/chat-scroll-back.test.tsx` ("scroll back in a phone chat"); mutations checked: each of the three slices restored, the per-kind start, the short rule for sessions, the view's lock, the phone count, the room drop and its remote count, the room view's `older` and its lock, the room's start rule and cap, a round's appends on the loop, a branch's and a resumed wait's keep, the round's count bound, the row read before the lock (session and room), the phone lane's window on the loop; on screen, the read-only rewind, the pinned guard, the place hold, the gap fill, leaving the bottom, retry after a failure, the started-over guard, taking the count with the view, the stale view, the first view's start-over, Keep, Undo and the review card on an earlier line, the room's press-only line and its words.

- **A tool result over a lane's limit is KEPT WHOLE for its own chat and read back in parts: ONE store, ONE reader, and the lane's old cut whenever that cannot be done** (v1.589.0, the intelligence plan, release 8: "long files are read to the end").
  The hard rule "keep big results out of the context" used to need the model to ask (`_store_as`, a script). It is now what every lane does by itself. `tools/kept_results.py` owns all of it; do not add a second place that stores an oversized result or a second tool that reads one.
  **The two steps.** `hold(ctx, content, cap, cut=, tail=, result=)` stands where the lane cut one result and returns EXACTLY that cut (a result that fits is byte for byte what it was); what it puts by lives ON the turn's own context (`waiting(ctx)`), never in a module global, so nothing of a result outlives its turn. `settle(platform, ctx, msgs, arm)` runs once at the end of the round: it first asks whether the reader may join (`arm(dry=True)`; nothing is written when it may not: no write-then-delete), saves off the event loop (bounded, `IO_TIMEOUT_S`), arms (`arm()`), and only then rewrites the tool message. Call sites: `chat_turn.kept_tool_message` + `settle_kept_results` in BOTH chat lanes (MIRROR NOTE; a coding session of Chat › Code rides the same two), and `agents/runtime._perceive_act_body` (`hold(..., tail=False)`, then `settle` before `_offer_script_tool`). The limits did not move: chat 12,000, coding session up to 32,000, agent run 16,000, and the rewritten message is never longer than the limit.
  **A save that fails leaves nothing.** `put` removes its own text, record, half-written files and empty folder on ANY exception (a record that cannot be moved into place, `_make_room` raising). The handle is made before the save (`new_handle`), so a save the lane stopped waiting for is named (`abandon`): it writes nothing, or removes what it wrote when it finishes. The message stays the old cut and no reader joins.
  **What the model is shown.** The start (in the chat lanes also the end, two thirds / one third as before, with a short `[… characters a to b are not shown here …]` where the middle was), the result's untrusted-data fence whole around it wherever it opens (`split_fence` is for LAYOUT only: a web page arrives under its title line), and ONE fixed line UNDER the fence: `[Iron Jarvis kept this whole result for this chat|coding session|run: N characters. Shown above: characters 1 to A[ and B to N]. To read the rest, call kept_result_read with handle "kr-…" and start (the character to read from); end=true reads the last part.]` (`NOTE_RX`). A copy of that line, or of the reader's own first line, inside a result is defanged (`defang`: `[` to `(`). When the context planner trims an old tool result to its marker it keeps a SHORT form of the line (size and handle, no "Shown above"), and only the one `settle` or `arm_at_start` put ON the message (`kept_line`, read by `context/agent_window.KEEP_ON_TRIM`), never one found in the text: a copied line in a result that was never kept is not Iron Jarvis's.
  **Trust is never read from the text.** `hold` reads `builtins.is_own_source(result)` at the call and it is saved with the text (`own_source`). A part read back is outside text (the reader is `returns_untrusted_content`: fenced, scanned, tainting on a hit, in every lane) unless that saved flag is exactly true. What a result starts with decides nothing: `web_fetch` and the browser's page fence (`browser/tools.fence_page_text`, a warning line first on a flagged page) do not START with the fence.
  **The reader.** `kept_result_read(handle, start?, end?)`: characters, counted from 1, a negative `start` counts from the end, `end` true (or the words "true"/"1"/"yes") is the last part, at most `READ_CHARS` (10,000) a call; its first line says which characters it returned and where the next part starts, every number written the same way ("17,611" is read back as a number). Read-only, `allow` by default. It is on NO roster, no words arm it and the lookup never lists it (`_OFF_ROSTER_BY_DESIGN`, `capability_search.index.NOT_FOR_CHAT`): `arm_chat` / `arm_run` put it on a turn's roster in place, never over the user's deny or a rule of the turn, outside a surface's `tool_ceiling`, or past a small model's tool budget (then nothing is kept). A turn that was not given it is refused by the registry as "not armed".
  **Whose it is.** Filed under `tools/registry.values_key` (release 1): `chat:<thread>`, a new chat's first message under its turn (moved by `rekey` from `tool_script.adopt_turn_worker` when the page links the turn mid-reply), `build:<id>`, an agent run's session id (a helper cannot read its lead's, nor the lead a helper's). The folder is named by a hash of that key and `get` looks ONLY there: a second chat, another run, a copied or guessed handle and a call with no owner get the one sentence `not_found(noun)`, which also covers a result past its date or replaced by newer ones ("read the source again").
  **How long, per seam.** A PLAIN CHAT's kept results last for the reply that kept them: a later reply never sees the handle (chat history carries no tool message), so `reply_scope` (the POST lane's `_kept_reply_turn` decorator) and `reply_frames` (the stream lane's `kept_reply_frames`) remove them when the reply ends, however it ends; a plain-chat turn outside one keeps nothing; a plain chat's folder is named `reply-…` and whatever start-up finds in one (a reply that never ended) goes. An AGENT RUN's and a CODING SESSION's last up to 30 days (their saved steps hold the line): `arm_at_start` gives a turn that STARTS with a line the store answers for (a coding reply resumed by the stream lane's `resume_tail`; a run continued with `options.resume_run`, whose old session's results `follow_resume` moves to the continuation) the reader from its first step. Removed with its chat, coding session or run (`routes/chat.delete_thread` AFTER it stopped the replies, for the chat, its coding session and each running turn; `orchestrator.delete_session`: REMOVED, never moved to the trash); a dropped owner is refused a save for an hour (`DROPPED_S`), so one already on its way writes nothing. Bounds: one result up to 4,000,000 characters, 16 results and 8,000,000 characters an owner (the oldest of EARLIER rounds goes; a round never pushes out its own: past the bound in one round the extra results get the old cut and a "did not keep" line, and `settle` checks every handle is still there before it writes a line), 512 MB in the whole store (`MAX_STORE_BYTES`; the oldest of anyone's, never one saved within the last hour; a running total, so the store is walked only when it is unknown or over the bound). `sweep` runs in the daily `daemon/app._event_prune_loop` and once BESIDE start-up (`_kept_results_boot_tidy`, a background task, never awaited in start-up).
  **Local only.** A result kept under the Local only scope is marked, and the reader hands it back only to work that stays on this network (scope on, no `allow_cloud_once`): a chat switched off Local only is refused in words, a cloud model allowed for one message is refused by name. WHILE a cloud model is allowed for one message nothing is kept at all (the read would be refused: the old cut's advice is the one that works).
  **A tool with a cap of its own: `read_document` and `extract_pdf`, and only these two.** Their answer is unchanged for every caller (the first 16,000 characters and `... [truncated to 16000 of N characters]`). When that cap cut it they hand the uncut answer beside it in `ToolResult.whole` (`documents/tools._answer`; the registry's read cache remembers it with the answer, or does not remember the read). `settle` puts the whole in the answer's place (`_with_whole`, off the event loop) only when the lane's message is exactly the LANE's fence round that answer and `detect_injection` passes the WHOLE (a whole that is flagged is never shown and never kept); a whole that fits the lane's own limit is simply shown, one that does not is cut and kept. A whole over 1,000,000 characters (`MAX_WHOLE_CHARS`: the scan holds the interpreter) is not scanned and not kept: the tool's own cut plus the "did not keep" line. Wherever nothing can keep it the message is the tool's own cut with its own words, then the lane's cut, to the character. Do not lift another tool's cap this way without asking.
  **At rest.** `<home>/kept-results/<hash>/<handle>.txt` + `.json`: the text the model was being shown, no rawer. OUT of every backup (`maintenance.create_backup`) and in no export; not `artifacts/store`. The keep step writes the text nowhere else: no log line (a failed save logs the kind of failure only), event, usage row or error. A part the model READS is a tool result like any other, recorded like every step (the ledger's first 4,000 characters, a step frame's head, a run's transcript), so it is in the database and in a backup; only the kept copy is left out (the owner's decision, 2026-11-26).
  **Not covered, left exactly as they were:** a file ATTACHED to a message (its block is prompt text; the model opens the file with `read_document`, which is covered) and an extension resource attached to one (`mcp_turn._read_one`, 20,000); every OTHER tool's own cap inside the tool (`web_fetch`, `run_code`, the script worker's print cap, `page_read`, a failed call's 2,000-character output tail); Build › Code; a run another computer's task started (its overrides deny every tool off `REMOTE_RUN_KEEP`); `attach_check`'s re-cut of an edit's message. A coding session does not arm `read_document` (its `read_file` reads documents whole). An agent run's fallback cut says `[... cut here: N more characters are not shown]`.
  A new LANE that cuts results calls `hold` + `settle` and arms through the registry's roster, never a page. Keep in step: `agents/mission._RUN_TOOL_WORDS` + `lib/runWords.ts`, `chat_turn._READS_ONLY_TOOLS`, `tests/test_leap06a_gate.LETS_RUN`.
  Pins: `tests/test_intel_08_kept_results_store.py` (the store, the reader through the real registry, the words, the two steps at the seam, the backup, the trim), `tests/test_intel_08_kept_results_lanes.py` (both chat lanes, a coding session, an agent run, an extension's result), `tests/test_intel_08_kept_results_replies.py` (trust from the call with `web_fetch` and the browser's fence, a reply's own results, restart on a coding session and a continued run, failed and timed-out saves, a chat deleted mid-reply, Local only, the tidy-ups) and `tests/test_intel_08_kept_results_documents.py` (the two document readers).
- **The agent loop prices the tool definitions each step really carries (serialised again whenever the list of tool names changes), and the OPTIONAL script tool is taken back when what it adds would not fit** (v1.595.0, idea 09 review, R2.20).
  `agents/runtime.perceive_act` kept ONE `_tools_blob` per invocation, but the script tool joins a run mid-way (`_offer_script_tool`, in place, v1.473.0) and rewrites the file tools' descriptions (~1,300 tokens on a builder; 727 beside `list_files` alone), so every step after it was planned against the first step's tools and went out over a KNOWN window. `_tools_names` keys the blob. Pricing it honestly turned a run that fitted into "too small" the moment the offer landed (`test_compaction_agents_v1153::test_a_run_stops_paying_for_compactions_that_do_not_help`, red on the full suite), so an offer is undoable for ONE planning: `_offer_script_tool` keeps `script_offer_undo` (the list, the tools before, the result the note went on); when the next step's plan at a known window clips the task or loses the newest block, `_withdraw_script_offer` puts the tools and that result back, sets `script_withheld` (no new offer this run) and the step is planned again; after that planning the record is dropped, so a tool a request already carried is never taken away. Still too small without it: the honest `ContextTooSmall`. Pins: `tests/test_agent_too_small_v14210.py::test_known_window_tools_trim_what_an_unpriced_plan_would_have_sent` (each request against its OWN tools, a tool joined mid-run), `test_a_script_tool_that_would_leave_no_room_is_taken_back_and_the_run_goes_on` (no request carries it or its note, every request fits the planner's own room), `test_without_taking_it_back_the_same_run_would_end_too_small`, `test_a_script_tool_that_fits_still_joins`; mutations checked: the withdrawal off, the note left on, the once-only blob.
